newsitem.title: USA: NRC, PSE&G to meet June 9 on N.J. nuke inspection.
newsitem.headline: NRC, PSE&G to meet June 9 on N.J. nuke inspection.

text.p: The federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said it will meet June 9 with Public Service Electric and Gas Co (PSE&G) to discuss NRC's latest inspection of unit 2 at PSE&G's Salem nuclear power plant.
The unit, in Salem, N.J., and adjacent unit 1, both rated at 1,106 megawatt (MW), have been shut for more than two years after the NRC raised concerns over the units' safety.

PSE&G must wait for NRC approval before it can bring Salem 2 back in service. The agency might allow a restart after a two-week review and evaluation of the improvements and conditions of the unit following an extensive overhaul.
PSE&G, based in Newark, N.J., said it hoped to receive permission to startup Salem 2 at the end of June.
At Monday's meeting, PSE&G will make a presentation on its readiness to restart the unit, NRC said in a statement.
Separately, Salem unit 1 has been tentatively scheduled to restart in the autumn.
PSE&G is the operator and a part-owner of both Salem units. Other owners include PECO Energy Co, Delmarva Power & Light Co and Atlantic Energy Co.
